sections.overview: This widespread tern belongs to the family Laridae.
sections.identification: At 47–54 cm long with a 126–128 cm wingspan, it is the largest and heaviest tern.
sections.habitat: It nests on open, sparsely vegetated islands or shores near shallow water.
sections.behavior: It may forage as far as 60 km from its breeding colony.
sections.reproduction: It nests in colonies, small groups or pairs, in a shallow scrape.
sections.ecology: Older sources use Sterna caspia; the current name is Hydroprogne caspia.
sections.conservation: The 2018 global assessment lists it as Least Concern and reports an increasing population trend.
